Knights of the Eigenrealm

Battle foes with linear algebra & calculus.
Solve to strike. Miss and bleed.
How it works
• Each turn is a maths riddle. A new topic starts gently: the rule first, then an easy one, then true-or-false, before you choose from four or build the answer yourself.
• Correct → your knight strikes. Faster answers hit harder.
• Wrong → the foe strikes you, and you're shown exactly why.
• Win gold & loot → forge better blades, plate, and relics.

🎲 Turn It Round

One question from a different workshop each time, with its rule stated first. Work it out, read why, then move on: mixing the kinds is what makes each one stick.

🏺 Area Workshop

An integral is the area rectangles close in on as they get thinner. Pick a curve, choose where each rectangle takes its height, then add more and watch the sum.

Things to find

🎯 Dot Product Workshop

The dot product of two arrows is one number that says how far they agree. Set u and v, and watch it, the angle between them, and the shadow u casts on v.

Things to find

👑 Eigenvector Hunt

A matrix knocks almost every arrow off its line. Pick a matrix, point v anywhere, and hunt for the directions that only get stretched: the eigenvectors.

Things to find

🧭 Span Workshop

A mix of two arrows is a·u + b·v: walk a of u, then b of v from where you stopped. Pick a pair, choose the amounts, and see which points the pair can reach together.

Things to find

⚖️ Elimination Workshop

Two equations, two unknowns. Change one row at a time: add k times the other row to it, multiply or divide it by k, or swap the rows. Clear x out of one row, then y out of the other, and the answer is left standing. Each row is drawn as its line.

Things to find

📏 Best Fit Workshop

Set a line y = m·x + c through a handful of points. Each point misses the line by its y minus the line's height there. Square every miss and add them up: the line with the smallest total is the best fit, the least-squares line.

Things to find

↩️ Undo Workshop

A matrix A moves the plane. Turn the four numbers of B until B puts everything back: follow î and ĵ through A, then through B, and bring both home. The B that does it is A⁻¹, the inverse of A.
B

Things to find

🔁 Order Matters

Do one move to the plane, then another. Follow î and ĵ through both to build the matrix for the pair, then see whether the other order lands in the same place.
First
Then

Things to find

⛰️ Downhill Workshop

f(x, y) = (x − 1)² + 2(y + 1)² is a valley with its bottom at (1, −1). The gradient ∇f points straight uphill, so a step against it, of size η, heads down. Pick η and walk: too small crawls, too big overshoots.

Things to find

🌫️ Limit Workshop

Some formulas give no number at one point. Close in on it from the left or the right, h at a time, and watch where f(x) is heading. A limit is what both sides agree on.

Things to find

🌀 Taylor Workshop

eˣ, sin x and cos x can each be built from powers of x, one term at a time. Add terms, move x, and watch the polynomial close in on the curve, fast near 0 and slower far from it.

Things to find

🔎 Newton's Method Workshop

Guess where a curve crosses the axis, then follow the tangent at your guess down to the axis: where it lands is a better guess. Step again and again, and watch a root run down in a few steps, or watch the method go astray.

Things to find

⛓️ Chain Rule Workshop

y is built in two links: u = g(x), then y = f(u). Move x and watch how fast each link moves: u moves g′(x) times as fast as x, y moves f′(u) times as fast as u, so y moves f′(u) × g′(x) times as fast as x.

Things to find

🏰 Two Castles Workshop

A hundred knights live in two castles, and each night some ride from one to the other by a fixed rule. A night is a matrix times the split, so many nights are a power of that matrix. Run the nights and watch the split settle on the one split the matrix leaves alone: its eigenvector with λ = 1.

Things to find

🔬 L'Hôpital Workshop

When a ratio gives 0/0 at a point, look closer: near that point the top and bottom are each almost a straight line, so their ratio heads for the ratio of their slopes. Close h in toward 0 and watch, and find the ratio the rule gets wrong.

Things to find

🌾 Product Rule Workshop

A field f(x) wide and g(x) deep has area f × g. Move x on by h and watch where the new area comes from: a strip down the side, a strip along the top and a corner. Close h in and the corner vanishes, leaving f′g + fg′.

Things to find

🪜 Ladder Workshop

A ladder leans on a wall and its foot slides out at a steady speed. The ladder's length never changes, so x² + y² = L² ties the foot to the top. Slide the foot out and watch how fast the top falls: slowly at first, then racing near the ground.

Things to find

🕳️ Null Space Workshop

A matrix sends each arrow v to a new arrow Av. Some matrices crush a whole line of arrows down to ⟨0, 0⟩, and those are the matrices that lose a direction. Set v by hand, watch where it lands, and hunt for the arrows that vanish.

Things to find

📐 Gram–Schmidt Workshop

Two arrows that lean on each other make a clumsy basis. Take copies of the first away from the second until what is left stands at a right angle to it. The right number of copies is the second arrow's shadow on the first, and taking it away is all Gram–Schmidt does.

Things to find

🧮 Geometric Series Workshop

Each term is the last one times r. Add them one at a time and watch the running total: when r is small enough an endless sum lands on a finite number, and when it is not the total runs away for ever.

Things to find

〰️ Bend Workshop

The first derivative is the slope. The second, f″, is how fast that slope is changing. Slide a point along a curve and watch its tangent: where the slope rises the curve bends up like a cup, where it falls it bends down like a cap, and where the bend flips over the tangent cuts straight through.

Things to find

🌊 Water Level Workshop

Pour the area under a curve into a flat tank of the same width and it settles at one height: the curve's average value. Raise or lower the level until the part of the curve sticking up above it exactly fills the gaps beneath it.

Things to find

♾️ Endless Area Workshop

Can a region that goes on forever have a finite area? Push the right end b out, doubling it each time, and watch what each doubling adds. If every doubling adds a fixed fraction of the one before, the area closes in on a number; if not, it runs away.

Things to find

🏺 Lathe Workshop

Spin a curve around the x-axis and it sweeps out a solid. Cut the solid into thin slices: each one spins into a disk, and the disks add up to the volume, closer and closer as the slices thin.

Things to find

🔄 Swap Workshop

u-substitution is a swap: trade a piece of the integrand for u, and its derivative for du. Pick a u and see what the swap leaves. The right one absorbs every x and turns the integral into one you know.

Things to find

⭕ Implicit Slope Workshop

A circle is not the graph of y = f(x), yet every point on it has a tangent. Differentiate both sides of its equation, letting every y term pick up a y′ by the chain rule, and solve for y′. Step a point around a curve and check each slope with a nudge.

Things to find

✂️ Parts Workshop

Integration by parts undoes the product rule: split the integrand into u, to differentiate, and dv, to integrate, and ∫ u dv = uv − ∫ v du. Pick a split and see what it leaves. A good one leaves an integral simpler than the one you started with.

Things to find

🔍 Eigenvalue Detective

An eigenvalue is a λ where A − λI crushes some arrow flat, which is exactly where det(A − λI) = 0. Step λ along and watch that determinant trace out a curve, the characteristic polynomial, and run down where it meets the axis.

Things to find

🗺️ Hillwalker Workshop

Stand on a hill and turn to face a heading. The slope that way is the directional derivative, ∇f · û. Find the steepest climb, the steepest drop, and the headings that stay level along the contour. Or walk a fence across the hill and find where it runs lowest.

Things to find

♟️ Cofactor Workshop

A 3×3 determinant can be expanded along any row or any column: each entry times the 2×2 determinant left when its row and column are struck out, with signs from a checkerboard. Every line gives the same answer, so pick the one that saves the most work.

Things to find

🙈 Cover-up Workshop

Split a fraction into simpler pieces. Clear the fractions and the equation left holds for every x, so choose x to suit you: where one factor is 0, every term but one vanishes and its unknown drops straight out. Keep the equations you want to use.

Things to find

🍞 Slice Workshop

A double integral over a rectangle is done one variable at a time. Hold one still and the solid under f is cut into slices, each an ordinary integral in the other. Sweep the slices from edge to edge and their areas add up to the whole.

Things to find

✍️ Slope Tracer Workshop

The derivative of a curve is another curve: at each x, how steep the first one is there. Step along a curve, mark its slope at each stop as a dot at that height, and watch the dots draw the derivative for you.

Things to find

➡️ Arrow Workshop

A vector is an arrow: how far across and how far up. Stretch one by a number k, walk a second from its tip, and see where you land. The straight arrow from start to finish is the sum, and Pythagoras gives its length.

Things to find

🌅 Horizon Workshop

Where does a fraction head as x grows without end? Step x out, ten times further each time, and watch the biggest power on top and underneath take over. Their ratio is where f heads.

Things to find

✖️ Cross Product Workshop

The cross product of two arrows in 3D is a third arrow, square to both. Turn v one part at a time and watch u × v worked out from the other two slots, check it is square to both, and see its length measure the area they span.

Things to find

➗ Quotient Rule Workshop

The slope of f/g is not f′ over g′. Step along a fraction of two curves and work its slope with the quotient rule, check it with a nudge, then try the two slips everyone makes and catch them out.

Things to find

🪃 Antiderivative Workshop

An antiderivative runs the power rule backwards: find an F whose slope is f. Guess F = c·xⁿ + C by hand, take its slope, and see whether the green lands on the gold.

Things to find

🪞 Transpose Workshop

The transpose Aᵀ flips a matrix across its main diagonal, so its rows become columns. Pick up each entry of A and put it down where it belongs in Aᵀ; a slot only takes the right number, and tells you why when it turns one away.

Things to find

🔑 Diagonal Workshop

To diagonalise A, build P from eigenvectors: then P⁻¹AP is a diagonal D. Choose P's two columns by hand and watch P⁻¹AP worked out, column by column.

Things to find

🎢 Trig Integral Workshop

To integrate sin(kx) or cos(kx), run the chain rule backwards: swap the wave and divide by the k inside. Guess F = c·sin(kx) or c·cos(kx) by hand and see whether its slope lands on f.

Things to find

🪁 Tangent Plane Workshop

A tangent plane is built from three numbers: the height at the point and a slope along each axis. Set them by hand and watch two slices through the surface, one along x and one along y, to see whether the plane touches.

Things to find

🪩 Inverse Slope Workshop

Arcsin, arccos and arctan are sin, cos and tan mirrored in the line y = x. A mirror swaps rise and run, so the slope flips. Step along, watch a point land on its mirror image, then try the two slips everyone makes and catch them out.

Things to find

🪵 Log Slope Workshop

In xˣ, x is in the base and in the power at once, so neither the power rule nor the exponent rule fits. Take ln of both sides to bring the power down, differentiate, then multiply back by y. Then try each wrong rule, catch it out, and add the two together.

Things to find

🛤️ Path Chain Workshop

A point walks along a path over a hill z = f(x, y). As t moves, x and y both move, so z changes for two reasons: the x part (∂z/∂x)(dx/dt) and the y part (∂z/∂y)(dy/dt). Step along and watch the two parts add up, then drop one or forget the speeds and catch each slip.

Things to find

⏳ Doubling Workshop

y′ = ky says y grows at a rate in step with itself, and that makes the same length of time always multiply y by the same factor. Pick a story, walk it a whole stretch or half a stretch at a time, and watch the curve against the straight line through its first two points.

Things to find

🪟 Trapezoid Workshop

Cut the area under a curve into strips and join the heights at their edges with straight lines: T = h/2 × (ends + 2 × inside). Double the strips and watch the gap to the true area fall to a quarter, over a curve that bends up and under one that bends down.

Things to find

🐇 Logistic Workshop

Growth with a ceiling: dP/dt = rP(1 − P/K). Step a population forward one unit of time at a time and watch it grow, slow down past half the ceiling, and settle on K from either side.

Things to find

🧵 Arc Length Workshop

How long is a curve? Lay straight chords along it, measure each by Pythagoras, √(run² + rise²), and add them up. More chords hug the curve closer, and the total climbs toward the true length, ∫ √(1 + f′(x)²) dx.

Things to find

🪡 Tangent Line Workshop

Near a, a curve and its tangent line are almost the same, so f(x) ≈ L(x) = f(a) + f′(a)(x − a). Pick a curve, step x away from a, and watch how far the tangent's estimate misses, and which way.

Things to find

📐 Chord Workshop

The mean value theorem says a smooth curve on [a, b] has, somewhere strictly between a and b, a tangent parallel to the chord joining its ends. Pick a curve, walk the point along it, and set the tangent's slope against the chord's until they match.

Things to find

👣 Euler Step Workshop

A differential equation gives the slope at every point but not the curve. Euler’s method walks it in straight steps: read the slope where you stand, move h along and h × slope up, and repeat. Pick an equation and a step size, take the steps by hand, and see where the walk lands against the true curve.

Things to find

🪴 Growth Integral Workshop

The short dashes show the slope of f(x) = e^(kx) wherever you stand. An antiderivative F has to run along every one. Pick the number in front of F and a lift + C, and see whether F fits the field. Then multiply by k or raise the exponent, as the power rule would, and catch each slip.

Things to find

💧 Cistern Workshop

A spring fills the castle cistern at a rate f that you cannot change, and the total so far is the area under f. Step the hours and watch the total climb as fast as the water flows, turn where the flow turns, and fall when the water runs out.

Things to find

🏗️ Biggest Build Workshop

With a fixed amount of fence or card, what you build depends on one length x. Change x and watch what it holds and the slope of that. Where the slope is above 0, more x helps; below 0, it hurts; so the most sits where the slope is 0. But check which way the curve goes on either side: a flat tangent can mark the least too.

Things to find

📈 Slope Workshop

A derivative is the slope a secant heads for as its two points close in. Pick a curve and a point, then bring h closer and watch.

Things to find

🛠 Matrix Workshop

Turn the four numbers and watch the plane bend. Nothing here is graded: it is for seeing what a matrix does.
